newsitem.title: FRANCE: French firms lament gap in net/gross wages.
newsitem.headline: French firms lament gap in net/gross wages.

text.p: A spokeswoman for France's small businesses said on Saturday that payroll charges need to be sharply reduced to narrow the gap between net and gross wages and allow French companies to be more competitive.
"We need reductions (in charges) of at least 30 to 40 percent," Martine Clement, vice chairman of the French employers federation CNPF in charge of small businesses, told Radio Classique.

"We have base salaries that are a bit limited, but extremely high wage costs. As a result, we don't properly remunerate workers, while the difference between what they receive and what they cost is enormous, and we also have a competitive problem with foreign companies on this matter," she said.

She said the gap between net and gross wages led to some categories of technicians and managers seeking to work elsewhere. "That's a problem we see more and more in the companies that have expanded internationally," she said.
